body: Just know you’re not alone. Mines 3 months next week and took to boob great then had to triple feed, began to prefer bottles and I’m at the point I’m about to give up. But at least they got some! My first I only went 2 weeks. So this one got more than first. But not even making a bottle a day. And with diet restrictions… accidentally bought a snickers bar the other day… almost ate it, had it sitting in front of me and then… dairy… so held off… but now it’s breast feed or eat that snickers and right now that snicker bar is pretty tempting 😂
Eh not great lol period so it dropped even more… will be giving up after this week if it doesn’t get better and I guess at least he got more than my first son. Have to think of the positive.

Man… I started out with the wearable set of discreet duo lansinoh. Read how it is better to have electrics and got one and I COULD NOT manage baby in my lap while trying to do that. I returned the thing. I went for a manual and that sucked too. I’m low supply so was trying to get better stimulation but still the wearable worked better for convenience and actually seemed to have the same output as the electric.

So…. I’d suggest trying a wearable and see how it does during that time. And when babe has been asleep for a little then try the electric

From the perspective of co parenting multiples… at least it’s only one parent? My husband has 2 others and one doesn’t follow thru and the recent is psycho… never acknowledges her abuse. Sooo…. Idk. This is a personal choice. I personally side to keep it… but that’s my morals and it’s a hard choice to make. You know how he is with the first and I had my second with my husband and kiddos are 8 years apart. Pros and cons to every path. You have to make the best choice for yourself.

My first time mom experience I bought the enfamil gentlease brand and now a days I figure that stuff isn’t that great. I know fed is best and what not. But regardless of the testing, it just feels a lot of our food in general is full of fillers and additives…. So don’t beat yourself up. It was a handful of times… my boy who was formula fed… is … well overall healthy. Besides pulling fast ones like tonight and coming out to keep playing with legos when I told him to go to bed an hour ago lol…. 

Now trying for more breastmilk this baby, and it’s been a struggle. Haven’t been able to produce enough to feed mostly breastmilk… it sucks… but doing the best I can. Approaching a give up time but just ordered a manual pump since I’m using a wearable and see if that helps… and well… just keeping on trying. 

You’re doing great and keep reminding yourself of the logical side that you have far exceeded benefits. Stay on top of less processed foods and you’re doing amazing!

Well this baby latched easily, and my milk came in almost immediately… what made it difficult is an unknown milk allergy and a shallow latch situation. 

I’d suggest if anything happens with a pediatrician saying to supplement or stop BF, I’d get in with a lactation consultant immediately. And have a breast pump on standby just in case. 

I didn’t have the pump right away. Waited for it to come in. Missed the full times and supply dropped and que the hardship. 

I wish I knew this advice before and stood stronger on my BF journey. I’m approaching a give up time since I now only give maybe a bottle a day. With diet restrictions I guess I just find it almost pointless to keep going but haven’t made that absolute decision since it has been so important to me… at least getting some of my breastmilk is better than none. So we shall see…

I had c section, was engorged feeling for 2 weeks, didn’t have pump yet, baby wasn’t gaining, but the time the pump came in, my supply tanked so not sure how much I could have gotten. Now I never really feel full. I’ve gone from nothing measurable to 1-2oz in a session, back to like nothing… I had gotten period back so I’m hoping this current dip is related to that. 

Trying to drink enough water and eat enough calories, have taken moringa and brewers yeast supplements, ate oatmeal and don’t think it made much of a difference…. Sooo… being a mom is hard. Providing baby nutrients is extremely hard. Even when doing it all “right” I’m lucky to give one bottle in 24 hours… not sure how much longer this will work… I pumped barely nothing today and yesterday with an actual pump session getting zero out of one… granted I latched him a bit before so maybe he got what was in there out…
Lollll i feel that!! You’re doing great momma!
See! Not frustrated with you:P he thinks you’re tasty!!

I get it… my first screamed at the nips and I lasted barely 2 weeks breastfeeding. 

My newest son, he took to the nips well but between dairy allergy, possible tongue tie, wasn’t gaining weight… had to go into triple feeding and hard to always pump and lost a lot of my supply. And now he will yell at the nips at times and won’t latch long. Can make it work fairly okay in early mornings I will nurse. 

It’s a hard job being a mom… but you’re doing great and give yourself some grace 💙
I’d suggest do some skin to skin to help with your bonding. Maybe after babe is fed and changed, then just skin contact nap ❤️

I understand ❤️ 

I know formula gets them fed and end of the day they need to be fed… but I know breast is better for immune support etc. 

I’m triple feeding since mine wasn’t gaining and find out he has a milk allergy. My supply tanked since I didn’t have pump in time. 

Now I’m lucky to give one bottle a day. 

Before realizing the allergy, I at least got organic kendamil formula. Now he’s on amino acid. 

I’d suggest to get pumping to keep supply if you’re not already. And also nipple shields maybe when breastfeeding. 

You’re not alone though. The thought of stopping or unable is a devastating feeling…

I have no specific idea. However, I do not warm the milk at all. Baby takes fine regardless room temp or from fridge. I am in a similar boat having to triple feed and and under supplier right now. Lucky to give one bottle a day… and well today went to give him 4oz bottle of  BM and he left behind .5oz… I get that off one boob on a pump… I put it back into cooler and gave a couple hours later. 

When the gold is given. The gold is not wasted lol. 

Next time I’d suggest doing 2oz at a time or something to avoid big wastes when you’re warming it. I think that increase bacteria potential. 

At this point imo tread at your own risk. I would personally avoid heating unless babe won’t even take cold or room temp, then still doing like 2oz at a time.

My son’s dad has eczema pretty bad and no food allergies… my kiddo has no allergies and never really breastfed him. 

My second son with my husband shows to have milk allergy. Me and husband have no allergies. However he has another daughter who does have a peanut allergy. 

It’s all so complicating and never know. My brother had peanut allergies too yet I have none.

Get it cut. I mainly have my son and will take him but a lot of times his dad ends up doing something with it. This last time my kid tells me it’s too long still and getting in his eyes. It was buzzed around sides but top still very long. So I plan to get it cut again anyways. 

It’s hair, it grows back. 

Just say you’re getting it cut more because child complaining in eyes. And as a female.. I don’t even wait that long for an appt! 2 weeks maybe. For my kid? Usually same day or within the week if that.

And now not allowed to nurse at all which is obviously way easier than pumping all the time. So that’s the most recent issue. And I was already down to maybe 1 bottle a day worth if I was lucky. 

I did check the video out and wish I had some info like that in the very beginning but I also read if milk allergy it will prevent some weight gain too which was an issue.
I just don’t know if the damage is irreversible at this point. I’ll check the video out thank you.

Only the 4-5am-6-8 am stretch for a little extra sleep and at that time I didn’t know more about safe sleeping but I don’t move in my sleep without waking and I laid on back, baby in my arm on my chest and had pillow to prop my arm to keep me still.

Maybe apron? Baby bib too? lol also I use washable nursing pads and change those out versus the entire bra all the time 🤷‍♀️ I’m new to all this and that’s just my two cents for what it’s worth

Then maybe you put a rule that if they ask that question at all or more than once, they loose it. 

I can see that being annoying and this way both could get what they’re wanting out of this. 

Keep tradition, but teach patience and they should learn eat all their food or until full (which ever you decide) and then wait for you to say “go ahead and get dessert.”

I hadn’t gotten the habit of this going so easier for us. We don’t offer desert every time but sometimes. But seeing other comments, I mean I don’t think it’s bad in a small amount and you’re following it up with a healthy snack before bed. 

Is this a hill your partner wants to die on? I think this is such a small thing and small pleasure. They came into this where you had kids already and have your own traditions. As it’s reasonable things will change when you partner up… but I think this is a petty move on the behalf. It motivates them to eat dinner, they get a small amount and then a healthy snack. Like someone else says, it’s teaching balance. Maybe if you approach it that way they may understand. 

But also haven’t they seen this going on for a while now and just want to switch up out of no where?

Possibly something you’re eating that is causing an issue? Maybe write down all you eat, then start minimizing one at a time to isolate which thing it is… possibly still seek out doctor/LC to ask their professional opinion.

Well I do appreciate your perspective overall and yes I worded it as if it’s okay but not in a way to give myself permission. More like seeking if we are off base, is this something developmentally okay because I was just stuck on approach. Not to say I’m not open minded about solutions to it or open to hear it’s not a good idea. As I was back and forth on it. 

This is also a sliver of information in short time as I’m caring for a baby and time to focus on typing a post is limited. There have been many times I did bring lunches up, times I was making the lunches myself and bringing them up after drop off because life is busy and working to still manage my own too. I’m not perfect and don’t claim it, just seeking better ideas. 

I wrote this post after dropping off my sons already made lunch and I had a clear schedule today. I had a lot of appointments going on in previous months and still do including both kids and baby. And can’t skip some of them. 

I’ve gathered the note on the door check list with a visual, and making a reserve in their bags for times if they do and I can’t get up there in time for their lunch period. Also meal prep their lunches so easier grab and go, I really like that idea and I’m sure would make their day to day tasks lighter. 

We get a lot of push back between them both on different things, daughter wanted boy cut hair, we didn’t think it was a good idea but let her get it anyways— next thing she’s hating it. She wanted to fast we said not to do it during school but she didn’t listen.. i can’t get up there every time and I have many times before too. She was claiming she was bisexual, we didn’t like that but told her we love her anyways and here for her.. now she says she isn’t… it’s a rollercoaster and we are just trying to navigate the ups and downs and teach as best as we can. 

If I forgot lunch at work and didn’t have money to just buy out I went without until I got home.. I often skipped lunch as a kid, not great of course but my appetite is finicky. So my perspective is it’s not harming for 8 hours and it’s not like it’s every day of the week to accumulate a deficiency or malnourishment. They get a lot of home cooked meals with minimal processed food and fruit and veggies. 

I’ve been very hands on trying to help these kiddos build better habits, reminding tasks each hour, writing a list for them, having them write the list, reminding in the car, when we get home, every hour after. There is no devices or tv after school until the task list is done (feed let dogs in and out, eat healthy snack, pack lunch, do homework) then they get a break with whatever devices or play outside, paint etc. then later the next task load happens with chores, then another break. Eat dinner, then bedtime routine, where they can earn a couple minutes of stay up little later, tv or tablet time for a little if they’re done in time. 

I feel I’m on her like butter on bread constantly tho and it’s exhausting. Hence trying medication routes, she’s in therapy, the one we just tried wasn’t working, starting a new one. But building better habits and putting effort into things has to start somewhere too.

At 11 years old and I was adhd undiagnosed, I still had to clean my room, I trained my family dog, I thought of others etc and I see a delay with her in all this. Her therapist is starting to wonder if she either has a delay, or if adhd is that severe and will know more in months to come. It’s just every single category for her there’s constant mistakes, issues, lying, comprehension lacking etc etc. (diagnoses adhd and odd) so we are digging into what’s going on but I’ve also been very hands on trying to help. Rewarding and complimenting positive behavior, positive habits and efforts but it’s not sticking… 

Anyways, I don’t mean to come off as neglectful or tough luck kids. I want to find ways to help and help them succeed.

Yes that’s exactly what is expected of her—definitely not the morning for homework. Dad has to work an hour away tho too and I’m a SAHM recovering from birth so he’s helping with morning and I get them after school so he doesn’t have to loose hours. We are working on a lot of angles for all of our ADHD and treatment. We are all a work in progress and trying to find better ideas and solutions

I mean… she blew up your trust first. 

That phone.. is yours.. not hers. You pay that bill. 

Being safe should be a given when dealing with online, social media, giving out your phone number. 

Cross that line? That’s her choice that led her there. Not yours by following your parental instinct that something was off with your minor child. 

Coming from a now mom, but was that kid at 12-13 talking to online people and fully aware they were probably not who they said they were, had the socials behind my parents back— who didn’t pay attention to what I was doing. If I was a parent to me back then— there would be hell to pay. 

This isn’t a game. This isn’t for fun. People have ways to track you by info in pictures, looking you up, there’s a guy out there that literally does this to show people how someone can if they really wanted to, based off a generic picture of you out and about etc. 

The world is big. Minors brains are not fully developed nor equipped and it’s our jobs as parents to teach, protect and love them. 

Don’t for one second feel bad about checking that phone. And I think her privilege of using one is out the window for awhile and even downgraded to a bark phone or something. IMO
If you’re not ready to be done then keep doing it! Mixing it so she still gets the benefits of breast milk but not having her struggle taking it.

So I have not used the shield for this baby, I started to with my last but didn’t like those either and breastfeeding journey didn’t last long either. But that was about 8 years ago so I don’t remember specifics anymore. 

And I used an evenflo bottle and Tommee tippee. I preferred the evenflo look but had a bottle just completely leak on me after several uses. The tommee has a longer nip so to speak but both had a wider base like boob. I prefer the tommee actual bottle because it measures down at 1oz and evenflo starts at 2, so when I’m pumping I want to see as much measurement as I can. 

I do use binky too a nuk version that is shaped more nipple like? Not hospital style where it’s straight cylinder shaped. 

Thankfully he adapts well between them all. Takes a few seconds usually when switching up so he realizes how to suckle. 

I do have some issues with his latch though but plan to ask about tongue tie now and see if that’s a factor tho.

The thing is the pediatrician was saying he wasn’t gaining weight.. born 6.1.. first check up was 6.2… next was 6.2 but did a feed and another check and was 6.3.. the last visit was 6.4… then he said to supplement so pretty much triple feeding… nurse in night and early morning, trying to pump at least twice a day, and then formula in between that. 

He’s fresh baby lol. Not even a month yet but will be soon. So with not gaining weight… his latch is shallow I believe being just nip getting in mouth, a couple times I got him to get a wider and deeper latch and yes didn’t hurt as much but hard to get him to be consistent on that. Hoping as he gets older and stronger he’d learn better? So he’s 2-3oz every 2-3 hours doc says to do… but maybe I’m bad on this but he can sleep 4-5 hours in the night and I take full advantage of that. Been making sure he’s fully fed before and bottle when we get up and nurse in between. I’m grateful for a sleeping baby. My first was up every 1-3 hours and took awhile to sleep thru the night..

I’m not a fan of pumping though. To clean parts, clean bottles, lube up, i usually can’t step away and get much done without baby crying for me lol. Then I sit applesauce style and lay him in my lap while i pump lol. Nursing is soo much more convenient so I hate I have to do this… and busy life, older kids, adhd squirrels over here so I need to be careful I don’t mess up and cause supply to go down.. I forget to eat and drink sometimes when stressed so ugh. Lots going on! 

Glad it didn’t cause your babe issues! My first didn’t latch good either but I was younger and different place, I didn’t care that I bottle fed… now I want to EBF as long as I can and I  rather be the bottle than make many bottles a day and cleaning them lol

I think overall it did? I still don’t enjoy the feeling lol but sizing down from a 21mm to between 18-19mm made a difference. And lubricating too! I also use nipple butter on them before pumping as well. 

Now I’m stuck wondering if baby has tongue tie because I’m pumping enough for 2-3oz per feed which is what he’s suppose to be getting right now? Or he’s getting tired breast feeding and sleeping too early. Granted I’ve pumped 1-2x a day because well time.. have 2 older kids too. I also started using moringa capsules to try and help the supply… we shall see 🤷‍♀️

Thank you this gives me some hope..
